raw.title: B2C Senior Marketing Manager Netherlands- Belgium – Remote-First
raw.excerpt: 🚀 Be part of a movement to change the way Europe pays In today’s digital Europe, payments still feel too complicated.
raw.description:
🚀 Be part of a movement to change the way Europe pays

In today’s digital Europe, payments still feel too complicated. Random delays, confusing rules, extra apps and accounts make it harder than it should be to pay and get paid.

The European Payments Initiative is changing that with Wero, a proudly European digital wallet to make payments easier, clearer and more secure. Online, in store, at home and across borders, with your money and data protected under European laws and regulations.

Wero is live in Belgium, France and Germany and launching very soon in Luxembourg and the Netherlands. Backed by 16 major banks and the two largest European acquirers, we’re building a brand new, proudly European payment system. Why not join us?

🔎 What's in it for you

Tired of marketing roles where you're just another stakeholder in a long approval process? At EPI, you'll be at the centre of one of Europe's most significant payment transformations.

As our B2C and B2B2C Senior Marketing Manager for the Netherlands and Benelux, you'll shape how banks, payment service providers, merchants and strategic partners embrace and promote Wero. Your work will directly influence adoption, awareness and engagement across key market stakeholders, helping build the future of European payments.

At EPI, we embrace a remote-first culture, enabling our teams to work remotely from the country they are based in, with in-person meetings at least once a quarter to foster collaboration and connection.

🐝 About the team

You'll join the EPI Marketing team, collaborating closely with colleagues across Europe and working with experts in brand, communications, partnerships, product marketing and market rollout.

You will act as a central point of coordination between internal teams and external stakeholders, ensuring that marketing initiatives, communication plans and market activation programs are aligned with business objectives and rollout milestones.

💥 Your impact

  • Lead and orchestrate B2C and B2B2C marketing and communication activities across the Netherlands and Benelux, ensuring consistency of messaging and execution across all stakeholders.

  • Develop and execute partner marketing programmes with banks, payment service providers, merchants and ecosystem partners to accelerate awareness, adoption and usage of Wero.

  • Build strong relationships across the payments ecosystem and act as a trusted marketing advisor to key stakeholders, aligning interests and facilitating joint initiatives.

  • Coordinate and manage marketing campaigns, partner activations, content development and communication initiatives targeted at B2C audiences.

  • Brief and coordinate creative, media and agency partners to ensure high-quality execution and measurable business impact.

  • Develop deep market knowledge and continuously monitor stakeholder sentiment, competitive activity and market trends to inform strategic decision making.

  • Track campaign performance, analyse market and customer data, generate actionable insights and continuously optimise marketing activities through a data-driven approach.

  • Present plans, influence decision makers and mobilise stakeholders around shared initiatives that support the growth of Wero across the region.

💻 What you'll work with

While we're less interested in specific marketing technologies than in your ability to drive market adoption and stakeholder engagement, experience with the following is highly valuable:

  • B2C and B2B2C marketing and partner marketing programmes

  • Marketing automation and CRM platforms

  • Performance and campaign analytics tools

  • Media and creative agency management

  • Market research and customer insights platforms

  • Microsoft 365

  • Digital marketing and content management tools

  • Data visualisation and reporting platforms

🕵🏻‍♀️ To succeed, you should meet at least 70% of these requirements

  • 8+ years of experience in B2C and B2B2C marketing, partner marketing, communications or related commercial marketing roles.

  • Strong experience developing and executing marketing strategies, campaigns, partnerships and communication programmes.

  • Strong understanding of the Dutch payments ecosystem, including banks, payment service providers, merchants and industry stakeholders. Experience in Belgium and wider Benelux markets is highly desirable.

  • Experience in fintech, payments, banking or digital platform businesses.

  • Proven success working within complex stakeholder environments and aligning multiple partners around shared objectives.

  • Excellent presentation, communication and storytelling skills with the ability to influence senior stakeholders.

  • Strong analytical mindset with experience using data and insights to optimise marketing decisions and business outcomes.

  • Ability to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution in a fast-moving environment.

  • Experience collaborating across international and cross-functional teams.

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Marketing, Business, Communications or a related field.

  • Fluent in English and Dutch (CEFR C1 or C2). French is a plus.

  • Thrive in a remote-first, multicultural environment.

🪜 If this looks like you, the recruitment steps are:

  • A first call with one of our recruiters

  • A team interview focused on B2C and B2B2C marketing, partner engagement and stakeholder management

  • A final interview with EPI leadership

  • Hopefully, an offer you can't refuse

⛔ Turn back if …

  • You're looking for a highly structured environment where every process already exists.

  • You prefer focusing solely on marketing execution without building relationships across a broad ecosystem.

  • You are uncomfortable working in complex stakeholder environments with multiple priorities and partners.

🎁 What we can offer

  • Remote-first culture with quarterly and annual all-staff in-person meetups to keep teams connected and collaborative

  • Possibility to work from another EU country for up to 3 months per year

  • Competitive compensation package, featuring salary, performance-based bonus, and a thoughtfully designed, high-quality benefits program

  • The opportunity to be part of a multicultural European company

  • Learning & development budget: €5,000 training budget per year

Otherwise apply!

🫶 Our commitment to equal employment opportunities

EPI offers the same job opportunities to all, without distinction of gender, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, social status, disability or age. EPI promotes the development of an inclusive work environment that mirrors the diversity of the clients our product is serving.

raw.description:
Joy & Grace is conducting a confidential executive search for a Chief Financial Officer on behalf of a growing, private equity-backed, multi-location operating company. This opportunity is being presented under the Joy & Grace brand while the employer remains undisclosed at the early stage of the process. The position is a senior leadership role reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer and partnering closely with the Board and ownership group.

Opportunity Overview

This is not a traditional controller-style CFO role. The organization is seeking a strategic financial leader who can drive financial performance, improve operational visibility, support growth initiatives, and help build scalable infrastructure for the next stage of the business. The CFO will serve as a hands-on executive partner across finance, operations, and long-range planning.

The company is in a growth phase and is focused on strengthening forecasting, improving decision support, and evaluating acquisition opportunities. The role includes meaningful exposure to executive leadership, board interaction, and enterprise-wide decision-making in a performance-driven environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Partner with the CEO, executive leadership team, Board of Directors, and ownership group to develop and execute financial strategy.
  • Lead budgeting, forecasting, financial planning and analysis, scenario modeling, and KPI development.
  • Oversee core financial functions including accounting, treasury, tax, audit, cash management, reporting, and compliance.
  • Provide timely and accurate monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting in accordance with GAAP.
  • Improve financial visibility into business performance, labor utilization, operational efficiency, and working capital.
  • Support mergers and acquisitions through financial evaluation, due diligence, modeling, and post-acquisition integration planning.
  • Manage banking, lender, investor, audit, and other external financial relationships.
  • Help optimize capital structure, capital allocation, and liquidity planning.
  • Build, mentor, and lead a high-performing finance organization with a strong culture of accountability and continuous improvement.
  • Oversee financial systems, reporting tools, automation opportunities, and ERP-related enhancements that improve decision-making and scalability.

Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate is a business-minded finance executive who combines strategic judgment with operational discipline. This person should be comfortable leading in a fast-paced, growth-oriented environment and using finance as a driver of enterprise value rather than simply a reporting function.

Preferred qualifications include:

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
  • CPA and/or CFA preferred.
  • 10+ years of progressive finance leadership experience, including senior-level leadership responsibility.
  • Strong FP&A, forecasting, budgeting, and strategic planning experience.
  • Demonstrated M&A and integration experience.
  • Experience in a private equity-backed environment strongly preferred.
  • Experience supporting complex, multi-location operations.
  • Industry background in construction, manufacturing, building products, industrial services, distribution, or similarly labor-intensive environments preferred.
  • Strong executive presence with the ability to communicate effectively with boards, investors, lenders, and operating leaders.
  • Advanced proficiency with financial systems, ERP platforms, reporting tools, and Excel.

Leadership Traits

Successful candidates will bring a high level of integrity, curiosity, accountability, and business partnership. The company values leaders who are analytical, improvement-focused, proactive, and comfortable challenging the status quo with data-backed recommendations.

Work Arrangement and Compensation

This role is remote within the United States and includes up to 25% travel for leadership meetings, operational reviews, board interaction, and acquisition-related activity. Compensation includes a competitive base salary generally targeted in the $200,000 to $275,000+ range, plus target bonus opportunity and potential long-term incentive participation.

Confidentiality Statement

Joy & Grace is managing this search on a confidential basis. Company identity and additional details will be shared with qualified candidates during the interview process. All inquiries will be handled with discretion and professionalism.

Equal Opportunity

The employer is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity of background, experience, and perspective.

About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

The Role

Define security architecture across BJAK products, applications, cloud platforms, and infrastructure. Partner with Engineering, Product, Cloud, Compliance, and Security to build secure systems and meet regulatory requirements.

What You Will Build

  • Define security architecture, patterns, and standards across products, applications, APIs, cloud environments, and integrations.

  • Own architecture implementation and ongoing alignment with SC TRM and BNM RMiT, including control evidence, reviews, remediation, and audit support.

  • Lead threat modeling and security design reviews for new products, major changes, third-party integrations, and critical systems.

  • Design and review IAM, privileged access, network security, encryption, key management, secrets, logging, and threat detection controls.

  • Review web, API, native mobile, AI-enabled, and data processing architectures for security and privacy risks.

  • Guide secure architecture across TypeScript/Node.js, Python, Swift, and Kotlin applications and services on AWS and GCP.

  • Evaluate security technologies, advise engineering leaders, and track remediation of material architecture risks.

What We Look For

  • Degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or related field, or equivalent experience.

  • 5+ years in security engineering, security architecture, or a related security role.

  • Experience implementing and owning SC TRM and BNM RMiT requirements, including control operation, evidence, and audit remediation.

  • Strong knowledge of cloud and application security, IAM, networking, encryption, secure design, and distributed systems.

  • Hands-on familiarity with AWS and GCP and architectures using TypeScript/Node.js, Python, Swift, and Kotlin.

  • Experience with threat modeling, architecture reviews, risk assessments, and frameworks such as ISO 27001, NIST, CIS, or OWASP.

  • Able to translate regulatory and technical risks into clear, actionable plans for technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

About Avaya

Avaya is an enterprise software leader that helps the world’s largest organizations and government agencies forge unbreakable connections.

The Avaya Infinity™ platform unifies fragmented customer experiences, connecting the channels, insights, technologies, and workflows that together create enduring customer and employee relationships.

We believe success is built through strong connections – with each other, with our work, and with our mission. At Avaya, you'll find a community that values your contributions and supports your growth every step of the way.

Learn more at

Job Description

Platform Engineer

Build the Platform. Automate at Scale.

Are you passionate about building reliable, scalable cloud platforms and eliminating operational complexity through automation? Do you believe in infrastructure as code, modern DevOps practices, and creating platforms that empower engineering teams to deliver with confidence? We’re looking for a Platform Engineer to help build, optimize, and maintain the cloud platform technologies that support our applications and services.

The Opportunity

As a Platform Engineer, you’ll help design, implement, and evolve the platforms that power our cloud environments. You’ll collaborate with engineering and cloud operations teams to improve platform reliability, streamline deployments, and enable scalable, secure, and resilient infrastructure.

You’ll work across modern platform technologies, including Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform, and Ansible, while applying GitOps, automation, and CI/CD best practices. This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys solving complex technical challenges, improving operational efficiency, and building adaptable platforms that meet evolving business and application needs.

Your Mission-Critical Responsibilities

Platform Architecture & Engineering: Design, implement, and maintain scalable cloud platform solutions using modern architecture principles and infrastructure automation.

Infrastructure as Code & Automation: Apply automation and configuration management practices to improve platform consistency, repeatability, and operational efficiency.

Containerization & Orchestration: Support and manage containerized environments using Docker and Kubernetes, enabling reliable deployment and operation of applications and microservices.

CI/CD & GitOps: Develop, maintain, and optimize CI/CD pipelines using tools such as Jenkins, incorporating version control and GitOps practices to support consistent, reliable deployments.

Platform Reliability & Performance: Monitor platform health, performance, availability, and redundancy. Identify opportunities to improve resilience, stability, and scalability.

Cloud Operations Collaboration: Partner with cloud operations and application engineering teams to understand application requirements and ensure platform capabilities align with workload needs.

Security & Risk Management: Implement and maintain platform security practices and controls to help protect systems, applications, and sensitive data.

Troubleshooting & Continuous Improvement: Investigate platform issues, perform system debugging, and resolve complex technical problems while identifying opportunities to improve reliability and efficiency.

Documentation & Knowledge Sharing: Maintain clear documentation of platform architecture, configurations, operational procedures, and engineering practices.

Technology Evolution: Stay current with emerging cloud-native technologies, DevOps practices, and platform engineering trends to continually improve platform capabilities.

What You Bring to the Team

The Experience: Proven experience in platform engineering, DevOps, cloud infrastructure, or a related software engineering role.

The Platform Mindset: A solid understanding of cloud technologies, modern platform architectures, and the principles behind building scalable, reliable infrastructure.

The Automation Toolkit: Proficiency in scripting and automation using languages and tools such as Python, Bash, Ansible, and Groovy.

The Container Foundation: Hands-on experience with Docker and Kubernetes for containerization, orchestration, and application deployment.

The Delivery Pipeline: Understanding of CI/CD methodologies and experience with pipeline automation tools such as Jenkins or Travis CI.

The GitOps Approach: A solid understanding of GitOps principles and version-controlled approaches to managing infrastructure and platform configurations.

The Infrastructure Fundamentals: Knowledge of networking concepts and services, including DNS, load balancing, and firewalls.

The Problem Solver: Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills, with the ability to investigate complex issues and develop practical, sustainable solutions.

The Technical Foundation: A bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.

Extra Credit (The Nice-to-Haves)

Avaya Platform Experience: Familiarity with the Avaya Aura platform and its supporting technologies.

Infrastructure Automation: Experience using Terraform and Ansible to provision, configure, and manage infrastructure.

Cloud-Native Engineering: Experience supporting distributed applications, microservices, and highly available platform environments.

Operational Excellence: A track record of improving platform reliability, reducing manual effort, and streamlining engineering workflows through automation.

Why Join Us?

Modern Platform Technologies: Work with cloud-native tools and practices, including Kubernetes, Docker, infrastructure as code, GitOps, and CI/CD.

Meaningful Engineering Challenges: Help solve complex platform, automation, scalability, and reliability challenges.

Collaborative Engineering: Partner with cloud operations and application engineering teams to deliver platform capabilities that support business and customer needs.

Continuous Innovation: Contribute to the evolution of platform engineering practices and help build more efficient, resilient, and adaptable infrastructure.

The pay range for this opportunity is from $127,100 to $160,000 + benefits. This range represents the anticipated low and high end of the salary plus bonus for this position. Actual total compensation will vary and are based on factors such as a candidate’s qualifications, skills, competencies.

raw.description:
About Snezzi

We help brands show up in AI answers. End to end.

When someone asks ChatGPT "which probiotic should I buy for my dog" or Perplexity "best whatsapp automation tool," we make sure our clients are the ones being recommended. Not through hacks. Through real content, technical fixes, backlinks, and measurement.

Founded by three operators who've built and exited bootstrapped companies before.

Backlinks still matter. They matter for traditional SEO. They matter more for AI visibility, because the models lean heavily on authority and citation signals when deciding who to recommend. That's where you come in.

The Role

You own backlinks. For Snezzi, and for every client we serve.

That means everything from high-effort relationship-led link building (guest posts, partnerships, digital PR, expert quotes, podcast features) to the systematic foundation work (directory submissions, profile creation, image and PDF distribution, citation building). Both matter. The first builds authority. The second builds breadth. Together they move the needle.

You'll own outreach end to end. Identify targets. Write the pitch. Send it. Follow up. Close the link. Track it. You'll build relationships with editors, founders, journalists, and operators that compound over time. The same contact who writes for one client this month should be open to a feature on another client next quarter.

The job is execution plus judgment. You know which links are worth chasing, which are a waste of time, and which will get a site penalized. You know the line between aggressive and risky. You stay on the right side of it.

What you'll actually do

  • Build backlinks for Snezzi and across all client accounts. 10-15 quality links per client per month on premium engagements

  • Run outreach end to end: research, pitch, follow up, close. Own the inbox

  • Build and maintain relationships with editors, founders, and writers. Turn one-off links into ongoing partnerships

  • Land guest posts, expert quotes, podcast features, and digital PR placements

  • Handle directory submissions, profile link building, image submissions, PDF distribution, and citation building at scale

  • Identify partnership opportunities: co-marketing, mutual mentions, resource page inclusions, brand collabs

  • Track every link. Domain rating, traffic, anchor text, context. Report on what's working

  • Spot toxic or low-quality links pointing at clients. Flag them. Get them disavowed

  • Stay current on what AI engines reward and penalize as ranking and citation signals shift

You're a fit if

  • 2-4 years of hands-on link building. You've shipped links, not just planned campaigns

  • You know the full toolkit: outreach, guest posts, digital PR, HARO-style platforms, partnerships, directories, citations, profiles, PDFs

  • You stick to whitehat. You know exactly what gets a site penalized and you avoid it

  • You're comfortable owning communication. You can write a cold pitch that gets opened and a follow-up that gets a reply

  • You're organized. Outreach at scale falls apart without it

  • You're familiar with Ahrefs, Semrush, or similar. You can read a backlink profile and spot the gaps

  • You write clearly. Short, specific, no filler. Editors reply to good pitches and ignore bad ones

  • Bonus: prior agency experience, D2C or SaaS clients, or your own relationships with publications and creators

You're not a fit if

  • You rely on PBNs, link farms, paid link networks, or anything that puts a client at risk

  • You think "scale" means blasting templated outreach to 500 contacts with no personalization

  • You want to plan campaigns but not run them

  • You're uncomfortable on email, calls, or DMs with strangers

What you get

  • Direct work with three second-time founders. No layers

  • Real client accounts from day one. Outcomes you can point to

  • A category that's growing fast. Link building for AI visibility is still being figured out. You'll help define how it's done

  • Remote, India-based. We care about what ships, not where you sit

  • Find and connect data sources: discover new APIs, databases, and enrichment providers that give our clients an information edge. You're always hunting for better data.
  • Architect CRM and automation infrastructure: HubSpot, Salesforce, n8n, Clay whatever the client needs. You wire it all together so nothing falls through the cracks.
  • Build AI-powered workflows: use LLMs (Claude, GPT) and AI agents to automate research, personalization, qualification, and analysis at scale.
  • Work closely with clients: run feedback loops, present your work, and translate messy business problems into clean, repeatable systems. You'll build real relationships, not just deliverables.
  • Push the frontier: R&D is part of the job. Test new tools, new techniques, new approaches. Share what you learn with the team. We move fast because everyone brings something new to the table.

Requirements

Must-haves

  • Clay expertise: you've built real things in Clay. Portfolio work, client projects, or personal experiments that show you know your way around the platform.
  • AI-first mindset: you use AI tools daily, not as a novelty but as core infrastructure. You reach for Claude or GPT before you reach for a spreadsheet. You're building with AI, not just prompting it.
  • Systems thinker: you see the whole picture. Data flows, dependencies, edge cases, failure modes. You design systems that are robust, not just functional.
  • Natural problem solver: when something doesn't work, you figure it out. You read docs, reverse-engineer APIs, test hypotheses, and find a path forward. Nobody needs to hand you a playbook.
  • Self-directed but team-oriented: you can operate independently and drive projects to completion without micromanagement. But you also thrive in a team, share knowledge openly, and make the people around you better.
  • Constantly learning: this space moves fast. New tools, new data sources, new techniques every week. You keep yourself up to speed because you're genuinely curious, not because someone told you to.
  • Technical connector: you can find new data sources, connect APIs, evaluate and integrate new tools into a client's tech stack. You're comfortable reading API docs and building integrations.

Nice-to-haves

  • Claude Code expertise: if you're already building with Claude Code, agentic workflows, or AI-assisted development, you'll fit right in. This is where we're heading.
  • HubSpot or Salesforce admin experience: CRM architecture and administration chops are a strong plus.
  • Agency or consulting background: experience managing multiple client relationships and context-switching across projects.
  • RevOps or GTM foundation: understanding of pipeline metrics, attribution, funnel analysis, and revenue operations principles.

Benefits

  • Competitive Salary
  • Work with a small, senior team that's building the future of GTM, not maintaining legacy systems.
  • Deep, meaningful client work. You'll see the direct impact of your systems on real businesses.
  • Exposure to the most advanced GTM tooling and techniques in the market. We're setting the pace.Real ownership. No ticket queues. No "just execute this spec." You design, build, and iterate.
  • A team that values builders. If you've ever felt like the smartest GTM person at a company that didn't appreciate what you could do, this is your place.

We care about what you can build, not where you went to school.

As part of your application, share your Clay tables: record a short walkthrough (Loom or similar) showing us what you've built and how you think about it. This tells us more than any resume.

For shortlisted candidates, we'll do a paid build challenge that mirrors real client work.

Who We Are

Imprint helps the world's best brands grow the lifetime value of their customers. We started with co-branded credit cards and rebuilt them to be smarter, more rewarding, and brand-first. We partner with companies like Crate & Barrel, Rakuten, , H-E-B, Fetch, and Shell to launch modern credit programs that deepen loyalty, unlock savings, and drive growth. But the card is just the beginning. We combine advanced payments infrastructure, intelligent underwriting, and deep customer data to create delightful and personalized experiences for members as well as efficient and profitable relationships for our brand partners. Our robust technology and world-class operations allow us and our brand partners to offer powerful financial products without becoming a bank.

In the U.S., co-branded cards alone account for over $300 billion in annual spend, and most still run on decades-old legacy bank systems. Imprint is the modern alternative: flexible, embeddable, and built for how people actually pay today. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Thrive Capital, Ribbit, and Khosla Ventures, we're building a world-class team to redefine how people pay and how brands grow. If you want to move fast, solve hard problems, and own real outcomes, we want to meet you.

The Team

The Growth team at Imprint is responsible for relentlessly driving the growth of our business, from setting go-to-market strategy to launching and running our merchant partners’ programs successfully and scaling their growth through new cardholder acquisition and existing cardholder engagement. We span business development, marketing, partner success, brand, and product, and work cross-functionally with the leadership team to be the voice and advocate for our partners

This role is based in Imprint’s San Francisco office.

What You'll Do

As the General Manager for a strategically important co-brand credit card program at Imprint Payments, you will play a pivotal role in building and maintaining strong multi-level relationships with our partner and ensuring the continuous and sustainable growth of the program. This role requires a strategic thinker with a strong background in partnership development, P&L management, and a deep understanding of financial services. This role will own and execute overall relationship and marketing strategies for the program, ensuring the program is meeting business objectives and goals for both Imprint and our partners. You will work cross-functionally with our internal teams and with our brand partners to execute innovative and value-driving initiatives that distinguish Imprint’s programs as top-performing across all KPIs.

  • Marketing and Promotion:

  • Compliance and Risk Management:

    • Partner internally with the compliance team to ensure that the Credit Card programs adhere to all regulatory and compliance requirements

  • Reporting and Analysis:

    • Generate regular reports on program performance and provide insights and recommendations to senior management

  • Cross-functional Collaboration:

    • Work closely with cross-functional teams within Imprint Payments, including product, risk, compliance, customer service, and finance, to support the success of the Credit Card program

  • Proven ability to play a client services role with demonstrated ability to marry the goals of two brands to drive mutual growth

  • Budgeting and planning - experience allocating marketing budgets, forecasting account growth, and leading annual and quarterly planning processes

  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to present in front of large audiences including executive stakeholders

  • Balance of creativity and analysis – the ability to turn data & insights into action

  • Experience leading cross-functional projects, with high attention to detail

  • Collaborative mindset - has a problem-solving approach with a can-do attitude

  • Excellent presentation and data organization skills. Proficiency in Google Workspace (e.g. Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive) a plus

  • Additional health coverage includes access to One Medical and the option to enroll in an FSA

  • 20 weeks of paid parental leave for the primary caregiver and 8 weeks for all new parents

  • Access to industry-leading technology across all of our business units, stemming from our philosophy that we should invest in resources for our team that foster innovation, optimization, and productivity

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.


The Role

We are looking for a Lead Recruiter (Corporate Functions) to lead hiring across Operations, Finance, Marketing, Creative, HR, Legal, Strategy, CEO Office, and other corporate functions globally.

This role combines hands-on recruitment execution with leadership responsibilities. You will partner closely with business leaders to attract high-impact talent, drive hiring strategy, and help build a scalable Talent Acquisition function capable of supporting BJAK’s rapid global growth.

You will play a critical role in shaping the organization by hiring exceptional talent while mentoring junior recruiters and establishing recruiting best practices across the business.


What You’ll Do

Business Recruitment Leadership

  • Own the end-to-end recruitment process for business and corporate functions globally, including Operations, Finance, Marketing, Creative, HR, Legal, CEO Office, and other key functions.

  • Partner closely with hiring managers and senior leaders to define hiring priorities, organizational needs, role requirements, and workforce planning strategies.

Talent Pipeline & Market Intelligence

  • Conduct talent mapping exercises across target companies, industries, and markets.

  • Develop strong understanding of global labor markets, compensation trends, and talent availability across multiple countries.

Team Development & Process Excellence

  • Establish recruiting best practices, interview calibration standards, sourcing frameworks, and hiring processes across business functions.

  • Review recruitment performance, pipeline quality, and hiring outcomes to identify opportunities for improvement.

  • Support the development and scaling of the global Talent Acquisition team.

Recruitment Operations & Reporting

  • Maintain accurate ATS data, candidate records, and recruitment reporting.

  • Track recruitment metrics including pipeline health, time-to-hire, source effectiveness, offer acceptance rates, and hiring quality.

  • Ensure a professional, positive, and consistent candidate experience across all recruitment stages.

  • Support compliance with local labor regulations and recruitment best practices across multiple regions.


The Right Fit Has

  • 5-8 years of full-cycle recruitment experience across multiple business and corporate functions.

  • Proven success recruiting for functions such as Operations, Finance, Marketing, Creative, HR, Legal, Strategy, Consulting, CEO Office, or other business-critical roles.

  • Demonstrated ability to hire senior, niche, and difficult-to-fill positions across multiple markets.

  • Strong expertise in sourcing passive candidates using LinkedIn Recruiter, networking, talent mapping, referrals, and other advanced sourcing techniques.

  • Strong stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence hiring decisions and challenge hiring assumptions when necessary.

  • Experience partnering with senior leaders on hiring strategy, organizational design discussions, and workforce planning initiatives.

  • Experience mentoring, coaching, or guiding junior recruiters is highly preferred.

  • Familiarity with global hiring practices, compensation structures, and recruitment across multiple countries.

  • Strong proficiency with Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) and recruitment analytics.

  • Excellent communication, project management, and relationship-building skills.

  • Experience in high-growth technology companies, startups, internet businesses, consulting firms, or fast-scaling organizations is strongly preferred.


What Success Looks Like

Why Join BJAK

raw.description:
SUMMARY

This position serves as technical expert in the subrogation claim representative career path. Under limited supervision, manages subrogation worker’s compensation claims with litigation, complex/catastrophic and/or coverage elements. Manages unique cases, where sometimes little precedence has been established. Serves as department leader by developing other employees and may function as acting manager in the absence of department management.

We are seeking an experienced workers’ compensation subrogation adjuster or bodily injury liability claims adjuster with a background in complex and litigated claims and negotiating settlements directly with personal injury attorneys and adverse carriers. Workers’ compensation subrogation experience is preferred; however, we will consider strong bodily injury candidates who have handled larger, litigated losses and are interested in transitioning those skills to subrogation.

This role identifies, investigates, evaluates, and pursues recovery opportunities and develops strategies to maximize recoveries. Candidates must independently analyze complex claim issues and understand, interpret, and apply statutes and case law to develop claim strategy and negotiate resolutions. Multi-state and multi-line experience is preferred.

This is a remote position requiring travel for team meetings 1–2 times per year and occasional in-person mediations.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  1. Independently investigates, analyzes, determines potential liability, and effectively settles with adverse parties.
  2. Recommends, plans and advocates a position on complex worker’s compensation subrogation claims.

  3. Develops and manages complex subrogation claim action plans to resolution, coordinates claim processes and approves claim payments.

  4. Supports the team by acting as back-up to other subrogation team members and manager and is manager’s or director’s proxy when necessary.
  5. Updates databases and prepares reports utilizing standard software.
  6. Proactively communicates and collaborates with workers’ compensation claims handlers.
  7. Negotiates and settles claims within authority, at the earliest possible point to bring cases to final disposition.

  8. Exercises independent judgment to settle cases prior to mediation and/or litigation.

  9. Obtains all necessary documentation from the appropriate parties within established timelines.
  10. Properly assesses the cause of action, collectible damages, and liability and expense exposures.
  11. Composes correspondence and various reports in the management of subrogation claims.
  12. Remains abreast of new case law and statutes affecting subrogation.
  13. Maintains confidentiality of information processed.
  14. Mentor team members on complex files and files above their authority.
  15. Works with Claims in participating in agent/client relationship management.
  16. Manages the administration of complex claims and catastrophic exposures, within authority, including claims generated from dedicated large accounts.
  17. Assists in the development of reporting, analysis and conducts education & training programs as it relates to subrogation.
  18. Represents the subrogation team on various committees and projects.
  19. Directs claims administration efforts within statutory, procedural, case law, contractual and/or philosophical guidelines.
  20. Provides leadership regarding case law understanding for subrogation team.
  21. Provides guidance and advice when required or necessary and encourage/motivate employees in their daily efforts.
  22. Serves as a technical expert for the subrogation team.
  23. Coordinates special projects on behalf of management, as assigned.
  24. Provides training sessions for team and/or other business units, as required.

Additional Responsibilities for SENIOR SUBROGATION CLAIM REPRESENTATIVE II:

  1. Leads catastrophic subrogation claims with large claim volume.
  2. Handles the most unique cases, where little precedence has been established, requiring innovative administration and problem resolution.
  3. May provide oversight to vendors.
  4. May take lead role in claim projects or initiatives.
  5. Conducts audits of claim files.
  6. Acts as liaison to claim consultants as needed to support enterprise initiatives.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  1. Relevant combination of education and experience may be considered in lieu of degree.
  2. Bachelor’sdegree in insurance, business or a related field.
  3. Continuous learning, as defined by the Company’s learning philosophy, is required.

  4. Certification or progress toward certification is highly preferred and encouraged.

Senior Subrogation Claim Representative II:

  1. Ten (10) years of progressively more responsible experience in a workers’ compensation subrogation or subrogation claims environment with demonstrated knowledge of subrogation, or in a claims environment handling liability claims, that provides the necessary skills, knowledge and abilities, such as experience in reviewing, investigating and closing the most complex workers’ compensation subrogation claims.
  2. Experience handling claims in multiple jurisdictions required.

OR

  1. Minimum of three years of AF Group Senior Subrogation Claims Representative I experience that includes independent handling of the most complex subrogation claims.
  1. QUALIFICATIONS
  2. To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

OTHER SKILLS AND ABILITIES

  1. Knowledge of subrogation process.
  2. Ability to manage multiple priorities and adapt to changing workflow to still meet deadlines and goals are essential.
  3. Ability to collect and analyze relevant information and based on the analysis make independent and effective decisions.
  4. Excellent customer service and organizational skills are essential.
  5. Ability to establish and maintain effective working and client relationships.
  6. Ability to negotiate with opposing parties and to resolve conflicts in a professional manager.
  7. Ability to maintain confidentiality as appropriate.
  8. Excellent oral and written communication skills with the ability to effectively communicate with providers, attorneys, agents, company leadership and policyholders.
  9. Ability to function effectively in a multi-functional team environment.
  10. Advanced knowledge of medical and legal terminology.
  11. Extensive knowledge of the applicability of relevant laws and regulations.
  12. Extensive knowledge of the appropriate laws, regulatory authorities, industry trends and their impact.
  13. Ability to understand business needs and conceptualize and implement processes and procedures that support business strategies.
  14. Demonstrated superior judgment and analytical abilities.
  15. Ability to prepare periodic reports as requested.
  16. Ability to research workers compensation and subrogation laws, regulations or specific issues, in order to offer guidance or direction to others.
  17. Ability to comprehend the consequences of various problem situations and address them.
  18. Ability to take a lead role and/or assist in training and mentoring others.
  19. Demonstrated expertise and superior ability in managing and resolving complex subrogation claims.
  20. Demonstrated leadership abilities.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by people assigned to this classification. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties and skills required of personnel so classified. This job description does not constitute a contract for employment.

WORKING CONDITIONS:

Work is mostly performed in an office setting with no unusual hazards. Minimal travel is required. Must be able to drive an automobile and have valid operator license. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, and ability to adjust focus. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to handle documents, books, manuals; reach with hands and arms; talk; and hear.

The qualifications listed above are intended to represent the minimum education, experience, skills, knowledge and ability levels associated with performing the duties and responsibilities contained in this job description.

Pay Range: Actual compensation decision relies on the consideration of internal equity, candidate’s skills and professional experience, geographic location, market, and other potential factors. It is not standard practice for an offer to be at or near the top of the range, and therefore a reasonable estimate for this role is between $82,9000 and $138,0500.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. Diversity is valued and we will not tolerate discrimination or harassment in any form. Candidates for the position stated above are hired on an "at will" basis. Nothing herein is intended to create a contract.

Pediatrics Admin & Front Office Support

Remote | Pediatrics | Part-Time, 30 hours/week initially | $5-$6/hour
Target Start Date: September 14, 2026
Future Schedule: Expected to increase to approximately 40 hours/week as the practice opens and patient volume grows

About the Role

We are looking for a highly organized, proactive, and adaptable Virtual Medical Assistant to support a growing pediatric practice during its pre-opening and early growth stages.

This is not a traditional, narrowly defined Medical VA position. During the startup phase, you will work closely with the physician as an administrative and personal assistant, helping coordinate meetings, calendars, vendors, projects, communications, and clinic setup activities.

As the practice begins seeing patients, your responsibilities will gradually transition toward front-office and medical administrative support, including scheduling, patient intake, insurance verification, and patient communication.

The ideal candidate is comfortable working in a growing environment where priorities can change, takes ownership without needing constant reminders, and can independently identify what needs to be done next.

Key Responsibilities

1. Executive, Administrative & Calendar Support

  • Manage and organize the physician's calendars, ensuring meetings, deadlines, agendas, links, documents, and preparation materials are consolidated in one place.

  • Attend administrative and vendor meetings as needed, take clear notes, document action items, and help ensure important follow-ups are completed.

  • Serve as a proactive accountability partner by tracking deadlines, projects, tasks, and outstanding items without requiring constant reminders.

2. Front Office & Patient Communication

  • Manage incoming patient calls, emails, texts, voicemails, and initial inquiries professionally once the clinic begins accepting patients.

  • Assist prospective and existing families with scheduling, follow-ups, basic questions, and other front-office communication needs.

  • Provide a warm, professional first point of contact that reflects the patient-centered experience expected from a pediatric practice.

3. Patient Scheduling, Intake & Registration

  • Coordinate end-to-end patient scheduling, including new patient appointments, follow-ups, rescheduling, and appointment-related communication.

  • Support patient intake and check-in by ensuring required demographic, administrative, and insurance information is collected accurately.

  • Maintain organized patient information and appointment records within eClinicalWorks (eCW) while following established clinic workflows.

4. Insurance Verification & Administrative Support

  • Verify commercial insurance coverage and determine whether patient insurance plans are active, pending, or require additional follow-up.

  • Complete insurance eligibility and benefit verification before appointments and document findings accurately for the practice.

  • Assist with insurance-related administrative tasks and potentially prior authorizations as clinic processes expand.

5. Vendor, Research & Project Coordination

  • Research vendors, clinic equipment, software, and other operational needs and compare available options based on cost, features, and suitability.

  • Organize research findings, pricing comparisons, project updates, and recommendations using spreadsheets and other tracking tools.

  • Follow up with vendors and internal stakeholders to keep clinic setup projects progressing according to established timelines.

6. Process Documentation & SOP Development

  • Document recurring workflows and administrative processes as the clinic develops its operating procedures.

  • Create clear step-by-step SOPs for tasks such as scheduling, patient communication, insurance verification, and other recurring activities.

  • Continuously identify opportunities to organize, standardize, and improve workflows as the practice grows.

Must-Have Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience with eClinicalWorks (eCW) is REQUIRED. Candidates without prior eCW experience should not be considered.

  • 1+ years previous experience as a Medical Virtual Assistant, Medical Assistant, Healthcare Administrative Assistant, or similar healthcare support professional.

  • Strong administrative, organizational, calendar-management, and task-management skills.

  • Excellent written and spoken English with the confidence to communicate professionally with patients, families, vendors, and healthcare professionals.

  • Strong spreadsheet skills and the ability to organize information, research, projects, and workflows independently.

  • Highly proactive and able to recognize what needs attention without waiting to be reminded.

  • Comfortable working in a startup-style environment where responsibilities and priorities may evolve.

  • Able to multitask effectively while maintaining strong attention to detail.

  • Comfortable using required secure networks, clinic systems, and productivity tracking software.

Strongly Preferred

  • Previous experience working in pediatrics.

  • Experience performing commercial insurance verification.

  • Experience handling prior authorizations for commercial insurance or HMO plans.

  • Experience supporting a physician, clinic owner, executive, or small medical practice.

  • Basic Canva or graphic-editing skills for simple social media or clinic content.

Tools & Systems

Candidates may work with:

  • eClinicalWorks (eCW) EMR, REQUIRED EXPERIENCE

  • RingRX or similar HIPAA-compliant phone systems

  • Google Calendar or other multi-calendar systems

  • Google Sheets or similar spreadsheet tools

  • Canva

  • Secure private networks/VPNs

  • Productivity tracking software

What Success Looks Like

You will succeed in this role if you become someone the physician can trust to take ownership of responsibilities, anticipate what needs to happen next, and keep important tasks from falling through the cracks.

You should be able to work independently, organize competing priorities, communicate professionally with families, and help create systems that allow the physician to focus more heavily on patient care.

As the practice grows, success will also mean helping create a smooth patient experience from the first phone call through scheduling, intake, insurance verification, and ongoing follow-up.

raw.description:
Who We Are

Imprint helps the world's best brands grow the lifetime value of their customers. We started with co-branded credit cards and rebuilt them to be smarter, more rewarding, and brand-first. We partner with companies like Crate & Barrel, Rakuten, , H-E-B, Fetch, and Shell to launch modern credit programs that deepen loyalty, unlock savings, and drive growth. But the card is just the beginning. We combine advanced payments infrastructure, intelligent underwriting, and deep customer data to create delightful and personalized experiences for members as well as efficient and profitable relationships for our brand partners. Our robust technology and world-class operations allow us and our brand partners to offer powerful financial products without becoming a bank.

In the U.S., co-branded cards alone account for over $300 billion in annual spend, and most still run on decades-old legacy bank systems. Imprint is the modern alternative: flexible, embeddable, and built for how people actually pay today. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Thrive Capital, Ribbit, and Khosla Ventures, we're building a world-class team to redefine how people pay and how brands grow. If you want to move fast, solve hard problems, and own real outcomes, we want to meet you.

The Team

The Growth team at Imprint is responsible for relentlessly driving the growth of our business, from setting go-to-market strategy to launching and running our merchant partners’ programs successfully and scaling their growth through new cardholder acquisition and existing cardholder engagement. We span business development, marketing, partner success, brand, and product, and work cross-functionally with the leadership team to be the voice and advocate for our partners

Location

This role is based in Imprint’s San Francisco office.

What You'll Do

As the General Manager for a strategically important co-brand credit card program at Imprint Payments, you will play a pivotal role in building and maintaining strong multi-level relationships with our partner and ensuring the continuous and sustainable growth of the program. This role requires a strategic thinker with a strong background in partnership development, P&L management, and a deep understanding of financial services. This role will own and execute overall relationship and marketing strategies for the program, ensuring the program is meeting business objectives and goals for both Imprint and our partners. You will work cross-functionally with our internal teams and with our brand partners to execute innovative and value-driving initiatives that distinguish Imprint’s programs as top-performing across all KPIs.

Key Responsibilities

  • Strategic Partnership Management:

    • Cultivate and maintain strong relationships with key stakeholders at our partner brand, including senior executives, marketing teams, and operational leaders

    • Collaborate with our partners to develop and execute a strategic vision for the credit card program, aligning with their business objectives

  • Program Growth and Performance:

    • Develop and implement strategies to drive the acquisition of new credit card customers while maximizing the value of existing cardholders

    • Monitor and analyze program performance, identify growth opportunities, and develop action plans to achieve program goals

  • Marketing and Promotion:

    • Collaborate with the brand's marketing team to create effective promotional campaigns and marketing initiatives to increase cardholder engagement and usage

    • Lead annual and quarterly planning, budgeting, and forecasting processes to ensure the successful delivery of program goals

    • Analyze market trends and the competitive landscape to identify opportunities for product enhancements and promotions

  • Compliance and Risk Management:

    • Partner internally with the compliance team to ensure that the Credit Card programs adhere to all regulatory and compliance requirements

    • Implement risk management strategies to safeguard the program's financial health and minimize potential issues

  • Reporting and Analysis:

    • Generate regular reports on program performance and provide insights and recommendations to senior management

    • Conduct in-depth data analysis to identify trends, customer behaviors, and areas for improvement

  • Cross-functional Collaboration:

    • Work closely with cross-functional teams within Imprint Payments, including product, risk, compliance, customer service, and finance, to support the success of the Credit Card program

What We Look For

  • 6+ years of relevant program and relationship management, operations, and marketing experience in financial services; experience in a co-brand credit card environment is preferred but not required. Experience in eCommerce and/or Sportsbook is also a plus.

  • Proven ability to play a client services role with demonstrated ability to marry the goals of two brands to drive mutual growth

  • Exceptional project management skills with the ability to handle multiple priorities and initiatives and execute flawlessly

  • Strong business acumen - track record of owning and managing P&Ls, with the ability to leverage data and insight to inform decision-making

  • Budgeting and planning - experience allocating marketing budgets, forecasting account growth, and leading annual and quarterly planning processes

  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to present in front of large audiences including executive stakeholders

  • Balance of creativity and analysis – the ability to turn data & insights into action

  • Experience leading cross-functional projects, with high attention to detail

  • Collaborative mindset - has a problem-solving approach with a can-do attitude

  • Excellent presentation and data organization skills. Proficiency in Google Workspace (e.g. Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive) a plus

Perks & Benefits

  • Flexible paid time off

  • Fully covered, high-quality healthcare, including fully covered dependent coverage

  • Additional health coverage includes access to One Medical and the option to enroll in an FSA

  • 20 weeks of paid parental leave for the primary caregiver and 8 weeks for all new parents

  • Access to industry-leading technology across all of our business units, stemming from our philosophy that we should invest in resources for our team that foster innovation, optimization, and productivity

Imprint is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status. If you are passionate about FinTech and eager to grow, let’s move the world forward, together.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.


The Role

raw.description:
SUMMARY

This position serves as technical expert in the subrogation claim representative career path. Under limited supervision, manages subrogation worker’s compensation claims with litigation, complex/catastrophic and/or coverage elements. Manages unique cases, where sometimes little precedence has been established. Serves as department leader by developing other employees and may function as acting manager in the absence of department management.

We are seeking an experienced workers’ compensation subrogation adjuster or bodily injury liability claims adjuster with a background in complex and litigated claims and negotiating settlements directly with personal injury attorneys and adverse carriers. Workers’ compensation subrogation experience is preferred; however, we will consider strong bodily injury candidates who have handled larger, litigated losses and are interested in transitioning those skills to subrogation.

This role identifies, investigates, evaluates, and pursues recovery opportunities and develops strategies to maximize recoveries. Candidates must independently analyze complex claim issues and understand, interpret, and apply statutes and case law to develop claim strategy and negotiate resolutions. Multi-state and multi-line experience is preferred.

This is a remote position requiring travel for team meetings 1–2 times per year and occasional in-person mediations.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  1. Independently investigates, analyzes, determines potential liability, and effectively settles with adverse parties.
  2. Recommends, plans and advocates a position on complex worker’s compensation subrogation claims.

  3. Develops and manages complex subrogation claim action plans to resolution, coordinates claim processes and approves claim payments.

  4. Supports the team by acting as back-up to other subrogation team members and manager and is manager’s or director’s proxy when necessary.
  5. Updates databases and prepares reports utilizing standard software.
  6. Proactively communicates and collaborates with workers’ compensation claims handlers.
  7. Negotiates and settles claims within authority, at the earliest possible point to bring cases to final disposition.

  8. Exercises independent judgment to settle cases prior to mediation and/or litigation.

  9. Obtains all necessary documentation from the appropriate parties within established timelines.
  10. Properly assesses the cause of action, collectible damages, and liability and expense exposures.
  11. Composes correspondence and various reports in the management of subrogation claims.
  12. Remains abreast of new case law and statutes affecting subrogation.
  13. Maintains confidentiality of information processed.
  14. Mentor team members on complex files and files above their authority.
  15. Works with Claims in participating in agent/client relationship management.
  16. Manages the administration of complex claims and catastrophic exposures, within authority, including claims generated from dedicated large accounts.
  17. Assists in the development of reporting, analysis and conducts education & training programs as it relates to subrogation.
  18. Represents the subrogation team on various committees and projects.
  19. Directs claims administration efforts within statutory, procedural, case law, contractual and/or philosophical guidelines.
  20. Provides leadership regarding case law understanding for subrogation team.
  21. Provides guidance and advice when required or necessary and encourage/motivate employees in their daily efforts.
  22. Serves as a technical expert for the subrogation team.
  23. Coordinates special projects on behalf of management, as assigned.
  24. Provides training sessions for team and/or other business units, as required.

Additional Responsibilities for SENIOR SUBROGATION CLAIM REPRESENTATIVE II:

  1. Leads catastrophic subrogation claims with large claim volume.
  2. Handles the most unique cases, where little precedence has been established, requiring innovative administration and problem resolution.
  3. May provide oversight to vendors.
  4. May take lead role in claim projects or initiatives.
  5. Conducts audits of claim files.
  6. Acts as liaison to claim consultants as needed to support enterprise initiatives.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  1. Relevant combination of education and experience may be considered in lieu of degree.
  2. Bachelor’sdegree in insurance, business or a related field.
  3. Continuous learning, as defined by the Company’s learning philosophy, is required.

  4. Certification or progress toward certification is highly preferred and encouraged.

Senior Subrogation Claim Representative II:

  1. Ten (10) years of progressively more responsible experience in a workers’ compensation subrogation or subrogation claims environment with demonstrated knowledge of subrogation, or in a claims environment handling liability claims, that provides the necessary skills, knowledge and abilities, such as experience in reviewing, investigating and closing the most complex workers’ compensation subrogation claims.
  2. Experience handling claims in multiple jurisdictions required.

OR

  1. Minimum of three years of AF Group Senior Subrogation Claims Representative I experience that includes independent handling of the most complex subrogation claims.
  1. QUALIFICATIONS
  2. To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

OTHER SKILLS AND ABILITIES

  1. Knowledge of subrogation process.
  2. Ability to manage multiple priorities and adapt to changing workflow to still meet deadlines and goals are essential.
  3. Ability to collect and analyze relevant information and based on the analysis make independent and effective decisions.
  4. Excellent customer service and organizational skills are essential.
  5. Ability to establish and maintain effective working and client relationships.
  6. Ability to negotiate with opposing parties and to resolve conflicts in a professional manager.
  7. Ability to maintain confidentiality as appropriate.
  8. Excellent oral and written communication skills with the ability to effectively communicate with providers, attorneys, agents, company leadership and policyholders.
  9. Ability to function effectively in a multi-functional team environment.
  10. Advanced knowledge of medical and legal terminology.
  11. Extensive knowledge of the applicability of relevant laws and regulations.
  12. Extensive knowledge of the appropriate laws, regulatory authorities, industry trends and their impact.
  13. Ability to understand business needs and conceptualize and implement processes and procedures that support business strategies.
  14. Demonstrated superior judgment and analytical abilities.
  15. Ability to prepare periodic reports as requested.
  16. Ability to research workers compensation and subrogation laws, regulations or specific issues, in order to offer guidance or direction to others.
  17. Ability to comprehend the consequences of various problem situations and address them.
  18. Ability to take a lead role and/or assist in training and mentoring others.
  19. Demonstrated expertise and superior ability in managing and resolving complex subrogation claims.
  20. Demonstrated leadership abilities.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by people assigned to this classification. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties and skills required of personnel so classified. This job description does not constitute a contract for employment.

WORKING CONDITIONS:

Work is mostly performed in an office setting with no unusual hazards. Minimal travel is required. Must be able to drive an automobile and have valid operator license. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, and ability to adjust focus. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to handle documents, books, manuals; reach with hands and arms; talk; and hear.

The qualifications listed above are intended to represent the minimum education, experience, skills, knowledge and ability levels associated with performing the duties and responsibilities contained in this job description.

Pay Range: Actual compensation decision relies on the consideration of internal equity, candidate’s skills and professional experience, geographic location, market, and other potential factors. It is not standard practice for an offer to be at or near the top of the range, and therefore a reasonable estimate for this role is between $82,9000 and $138,0500.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. Diversity is valued and we will not tolerate discrimination or harassment in any form. Candidates for the position stated above are hired on an "at will" basis. Nothing herein is intended to create a contract.

Pediatrics Admin & Front Office Support

Remote | Pediatrics | Part-Time, 30 hours/week initially | $5-$6/hour
Target Start Date: September 14, 2026
Future Schedule: Expected to increase to approximately 40 hours/week as the practice opens and patient volume grows

About the Role

We are looking for a highly organized, proactive, and adaptable Virtual Medical Assistant to support a growing pediatric practice during its pre-opening and early growth stages.

This is not a traditional, narrowly defined Medical VA position. During the startup phase, you will work closely with the physician as an administrative and personal assistant, helping coordinate meetings, calendars, vendors, projects, communications, and clinic setup activities.

As the practice begins seeing patients, your responsibilities will gradually transition toward front-office and medical administrative support, including scheduling, patient intake, insurance verification, and patient communication.

The ideal candidate is comfortable working in a growing environment where priorities can change, takes ownership without needing constant reminders, and can independently identify what needs to be done next.

Key Responsibilities

1. Executive, Administrative & Calendar Support

  • Manage and organize the physician's calendars, ensuring meetings, deadlines, agendas, links, documents, and preparation materials are consolidated in one place.

  • Attend administrative and vendor meetings as needed, take clear notes, document action items, and help ensure important follow-ups are completed.

  • Serve as a proactive accountability partner by tracking deadlines, projects, tasks, and outstanding items without requiring constant reminders.

2. Front Office & Patient Communication

  • Manage incoming patient calls, emails, texts, voicemails, and initial inquiries professionally once the clinic begins accepting patients.

  • Assist prospective and existing families with scheduling, follow-ups, basic questions, and other front-office communication needs.

  • Provide a warm, professional first point of contact that reflects the patient-centered experience expected from a pediatric practice.

3. Patient Scheduling, Intake & Registration

  • Coordinate end-to-end patient scheduling, including new patient appointments, follow-ups, rescheduling, and appointment-related communication.

  • Support patient intake and check-in by ensuring required demographic, administrative, and insurance information is collected accurately.

  • Maintain organized patient information and appointment records within eClinicalWorks (eCW) while following established clinic workflows.

4. Insurance Verification & Administrative Support

  • Verify commercial insurance coverage and determine whether patient insurance plans are active, pending, or require additional follow-up.

  • Complete insurance eligibility and benefit verification before appointments and document findings accurately for the practice.

  • Assist with insurance-related administrative tasks and potentially prior authorizations as clinic processes expand.

5. Vendor, Research & Project Coordination

  • Research vendors, clinic equipment, software, and other operational needs and compare available options based on cost, features, and suitability.

  • Organize research findings, pricing comparisons, project updates, and recommendations using spreadsheets and other tracking tools.

  • Follow up with vendors and internal stakeholders to keep clinic setup projects progressing according to established timelines.

6. Process Documentation & SOP Development

  • Document recurring workflows and administrative processes as the clinic develops its operating procedures.

  • Create clear step-by-step SOPs for tasks such as scheduling, patient communication, insurance verification, and other recurring activities.

  • Continuously identify opportunities to organize, standardize, and improve workflows as the practice grows.

Must-Have Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience with eClinicalWorks (eCW) is REQUIRED. Candidates without prior eCW experience should not be considered.

  • 1+ years previous experience as a Medical Virtual Assistant, Medical Assistant, Healthcare Administrative Assistant, or similar healthcare support professional.

  • Strong administrative, organizational, calendar-management, and task-management skills.

  • Excellent written and spoken English with the confidence to communicate professionally with patients, families, vendors, and healthcare professionals.

  • Strong spreadsheet skills and the ability to organize information, research, projects, and workflows independently.

  • Highly proactive and able to recognize what needs attention without waiting to be reminded.

  • Comfortable working in a startup-style environment where responsibilities and priorities may evolve.

  • Able to multitask effectively while maintaining strong attention to detail.

  • Comfortable using required secure networks, clinic systems, and productivity tracking software.

Strongly Preferred

  • Previous experience working in pediatrics.

  • Experience performing commercial insurance verification.

  • Experience handling prior authorizations for commercial insurance or HMO plans.

  • Experience supporting a physician, clinic owner, executive, or small medical practice.

  • Basic Canva or graphic-editing skills for simple social media or clinic content.

Tools & Systems

Candidates may work with:

  • eClinicalWorks (eCW) EMR, REQUIRED EXPERIENCE

  • RingRX or similar HIPAA-compliant phone systems

  • Google Calendar or other multi-calendar systems

  • Google Sheets or similar spreadsheet tools

  • Canva

  • Secure private networks/VPNs

  • Productivity tracking software

What Success Looks Like

You will succeed in this role if you become someone the physician can trust to take ownership of responsibilities, anticipate what needs to happen next, and keep important tasks from falling through the cracks.

You should be able to work independently, organize competing priorities, communicate professionally with families, and help create systems that allow the physician to focus more heavily on patient care.

As the practice grows, success will also mean helping create a smooth patient experience from the first phone call through scheduling, intake, insurance verification, and ongoing follow-up.
